extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent applicants, patent attorneys and agents
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules from the MPEP governing Defensive Publications/abstracts/abbreviatures as prior art and the scheduling, conduct, recordation, and limitations of interviews between applicants/representatives and patent examiners (including use of video conferencing, e-mail, and related forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive Publication status as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A defensive publication is not a patent or an application publication under 35 U.S.C. 122(b); it is a publication. Therefore, it is prior art only as of its publication date. See MPEP § 2136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Defensive Publication Abstract and a selected figure (if any) were published in the Official Gazette. Defensive Publications may be used alone or in combination with other prior art in rejecting claims under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Defensive Publication on benefit of earlier filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: An application laid open under the Defensive Publication Program and provisionally abandoned retained interference rights for a limited period but defensive publication precluded a continuing application filed under 35 U.S.C. 120 from being entitled to the benefit of the filing date of the defensively published application unless a continuing application was filed within 30 months after the earliest effective U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a first continuing application was filed within 30 months, later copending continuing applications were not barred even if filed beyond 30 months; if similar application filed after 30 months, it was examined but not entitled to claim the earlier filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviatures and abstracts as publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviatures were prepared and published in accordance with the Notice of October 13, 1964. Each abbreviature contains a specific portion of the disclosure, preferably a detailed representative claim, and, where drawings exist, a figure. The publication of such abbreviatures was discontinued in 1965.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts and Abbreviatures are cited under 'Other References' and are prior art effective from their publication date in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for abstracts, abbreviatures, and defensive publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts and Abbreviatures and Defensive Publications must be referred to as publications and cited as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) or 102(b) effective from the date of publication in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example citation formats are provided (e.g., 'Brown, (abstract or abbreviature) of Serial No. ..., published in O.G. ..., on ... (list classification)') and Defensive Publications are listed with 'U.S. Patent Documents'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application portions used as reference only for evidence of prior knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: An application or portion thereof from which an abstract, abbreviature or defensive publication has been prepared may be used as a reference under 35 U.S.C. 102(a), effective from the actual date of filing in the United States, only for evidence of prior knowledge of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such applications (or portions) may be used alone or in combination with other prior art in rejecting claims under 102 and 103; see Ex parte Osmond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive Publication numbering and file maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct numbers are assigned to Defensive Publications published in various periods; conversion tables exist for older publications, and the defensive publication application files are maintained in the File Information Unit (Record Room).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct numbers are used for official reference and document copy requirements; Defensive Publications are included in subclass lists and subscription orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an interview
rubrics_metrics.description: The personal appearance of an applicant, attorney, or agent before the examiner or a telephone conversation or video conference or electronic mail between such parties presenting matters for the examiner’s consideration is considered an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews encompass in-person, telephonic, video conference, and electronic mail communications when substantive matters are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews concerning applications and other matters pending before the Office must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours, as the respective examiners may designate. Interviews will not be permitted at any other time or place without the authority of the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible locations include examiner offices, conference rooms, or the Video Conference Center; interviews are permissible during normal business hours Monday–Friday except hours when examiner is working overtime.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interview on patentability before first Office action except continuing/substitute applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview for the discussion of the patentability of a pending application will not occur before the first Office action, unless the application is a continuing or substitute application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for pre-first-action interviews in other applications are ordinarily untimely and will not be acknowledged or granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may require that an interview be scheduled in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may require that an interview be scheduled in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling in advance allows the examiner to prepare; applicant-initiated interview requests should use form PTOL-413A to identify participants, proposed date/time, type (telephonic, personal, video), exhibits, and issues to be discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statement required when reconsideration is requested after interview
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance where reconsideration is requested in view of an interview with an examiner, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview does not remove the necessity for reply to Office actions (§§1.111 and 1.135). The substance of any interview must be made of record in the application (see MPEP §502.03 and §713.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet e-mail restrictions for interview-like communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet e-mail shall NOT be used to conduct an exchange or communications similar to those exchanged during telephone or personal interviews unless a written authorization from the applicants or an attorney/agent of record has been given to use Internet e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When authorized, a paper copy of the Internet e-mail contents MUST be made and placed in the patent application file as required by the Federal Records Act, in the same manner as an Examiner Interview Summary form is entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Conference Center (VCC) usage and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO has established a Video Conference Center administered by the Office of Patent Training available for authorized official business during normal hours; use is currently limited to partnership PTDLs with duplicate equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customers should contact the patent examiner and identify two alternative dates/times. The examiner will coordinate arrangements with Office of Patent Training; VCC interviews must be arranged at least 3 days in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange interviews in advance and use PTOL-413A (Applicant Initiated Interview Request)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should normally be arranged in advance, and when applicant initiates a request, an 'Applicant Initiated Interview Request' form (PTOL-413A) should be submitted to the examiner prior to the interview so the examiner can prepare and focus on issues to be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-413A should identify participants, proposed date/time, interview type, a brief description of issues, and proposed exhibits. Failure to submit the form does not, by itself, justify denying the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexpected or surprise interview may be refused
rubrics_metrics.description: The unexpected appearance of an attorney or applicant requesting an interview without any previous notice to the examiner may well justify his or her refusal of the interview at that time, particularly in an involved case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior arrangement helps ensure primary examiner and other necessary participants are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews should be used only to develop/clarify specific issues and advance prosecution; applicant must be prepared
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should be had only when the nature of the case is such that the interview could serve to develop and clarify specific issues and lead to a mutual understanding between the examiner and the applicant, and thereby advance the prosecution of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attorney should be fully prepared to discuss issues raised in the Office action and preferably indicate in advance what issues are to be discussed by submitting a proposed amendment; if not prepared, interview should not be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners should avoid unnecessary interruptions during interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should avoid unnecessary interruptions during interviews with attorneys or inventors and should not take incoming telephone calls unless of an emergency nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should familiarize themselves with the status and existing issues before the interview; the examiner may state that further search/study is needed or conclude the interview if no common ground can be reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable interview duration (usually not longer than 30 minutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of both parties to the interview to see that it is not extended beyond a reasonable period, usually not longer than 30 minutes. It is the duty of the primary examiner to see that an interview is not extended beyond a reasonable period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties should manage time; interviews for unrepresented applicants should not be overly long.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substance of any interview must be made of record
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete written statement as to the substance of any face-to-face, video conference, electronic mail or telephone interview with regard to the merits of an application must be made of record in the application, whether or not an agreement was reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is under 37 CFR 1.133(b) and MPEP §502.03. If the examiner initiated the interview and indicated on PTOL-413B that the examiner will provide a written summary, the applicant's responsibility to draft may be reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum content required for complete recordation of interview substance (A–H)
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete and proper recordation of the substance of any interview should include at least the following applicable items: (A) description of any exhibit/demonstration; (B) identification of claims discussed; (C) identification of specific prior art discussed; (D) identification of principal proposed substantive amendments; (E) identification of principal thrust arguments of applicant and examiner; (F) general indication of other pertinent matters discussed; (G) general results or outcome; (H) for electronic mail, a paper copy of the e-mail contents must be placed in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The identification of arguments need not be verbatim or highly detailed; it need only convey the general nature or thrust so the file context is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must complete Interview Summary (PTOL-413) when substance discussed; PTOL-413B for examiner-initiated interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must complete an Interview Summary form PTOL-413 for each interview where a matter of substance has been discussed by checking appropriate boxes and filling in the blanks. If the examiner initiated the interview, the examiner should complete part I of PTOL-413B in advance and parts II and III at conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The completed PTOL-413 or PTOL-413B should be given a paper number, placed in the file, listed on the Content list, and a duplicate copy provided to the applicant (or mailed/faxed for telephonic/e-mail/video).

rubrics_metrics.name: PTOL-413 form information fields (A–L)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTOL-413 form provides for recordation of: (A) application number; (B) name of applicant; (C) name of examiner; (D) date of interview; (E) type of interview; (F) names of participants; (G) whether an exhibit was shown; (H) identification of claims discussed; (I) identification of specific prior art discussed; (J) whether an agreement was reached and description; (K) signature of examiner; (L) names of other USPTO personnel present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form also contains a statement reminding the applicant of responsibility to record the substance of the interview and instructions on distribution and placement in the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's responsibility to record interview substance and examiner review
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of the applicant or the attorney or agent to make the substance of an interview of record in the application file, except where the interview was initiated by the examiner and the examiner indicated on PTOL-413B that the examiner will provide a written summary. Examiners are expected to carefully review the applicant’s record of the substance of an interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record is not complete or accurate and it bears directly on patentability, the examiner may give the applicant one month to complete/correct the record under 37 CFR 1.135(c) when the record is in reply to a nonfinal Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when applicant's interview record is inaccurate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant’s summary attributes statements to the examiner that are inaccurate and the inaccuracy bears directly on the question of patentability, it should be pointed out in the next Office letter. If claims are allowable for other reasons, the examiner should send a letter setting forth his or her version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record is accurate, the examiner should annotate the paper recording with 'Interview record OK', date, and initials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video tape viewing during interviews requires prior supervisory approval and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys or applicants wishing to show a video tape during an examiner interview must demonstrate that the tape bears on an outstanding issue and that viewing will advance prosecution. Prior approval by the supervisory patent examiner and use authorization by the Office of Patent Training is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should be made at least 1 week in advance. Viewing using Office equipment will be held only in Office of Patent Training facilities and the substance of the interview including a summary of the tape must be made of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners may grant one interview after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may grant one interview after final rejection. See MPEP §713.09.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an exception to the general limitation on interviews after certain prosecution stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a reply requests an interview, examiner should grant if it will expedite to final action
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reply to a first complete action includes a request for an interview, a telephone consultation to be initiated by the examiner or a video conference, the examiner should grant such request if it appears that the interview or consultation would result in expediting the case to a final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agreement is reached, applicant should promptly submit an amendment; the examiner should consider taking the case up as special if the amendment readies the case for final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination continued by a different examiner should respect interview agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner who conducted the interview is replaced and there is indication an interview had been held, the second examiner should ascertain any agreements reached. Where conditions permit, the second examiner should take a position consistent with the agreements previously reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies unless there is a clear error or knowledge of other prior art; see MPEP §812.01 for telephone practice in restriction/election situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prior to filing and 'sounding out' interviews are restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing, no interview is permitted, except a limited amount of time may be spent indicating the field of search. Interviews solely for the purpose of 'sounding out' the examiner are not permitted when any agreement would be conditional upon being satisfactory to the principal attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for an interview prior to the first Office action is ordinarily granted only in continuing or substitute applications; otherwise it is untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and power to conduct interviews — who may be granted interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are not generally granted to persons who lack proper authority from the applicant or attorney/agent of record in the form of a paper on file in the application. A mere power to inspect is not sufficient authority for granting an interview involving the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews generally should not be granted unless the requesting party has authority to bind the principal. Registered local representatives should have a power of attorney of record. Practitioners cannot authorize other practitioners or nonpractitioners to conduct interviews without meeting ethical/regulatory requirements (37 CFR 10.57(c), 10.47).

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone interviews and examiner-initiated contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Office policy places great emphasis on telephone interviews initiated by the examiner to attorneys and agents of record. The examiner, by telephone, may suggest minor changes likely to result in allowance or may state major questions concisely and suggest a further interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone calls should be made via the Office telephone system; if a lengthy discussion is needed, the call may be terminated with an agreement for a callback at a specified time.

rubrics_metrics.name: For interviews where the conducting examiner lacks negotiation authority include an authorized examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: For an interview with an examiner who does not have negotiation authority, arrangements should always include an examiner who does have such authority and who is familiar with the application so that authoritative agreement may be reached at the time of the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that any agreements reached are binding and informed.
